subject: Customer plan: resident snapshots, customer-led erase, evidence for compliance
messages:
From: Diana Lee <diana.lee@medicarehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: it-security@medicarehealth.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on snapshots, regional retention, and customer-initiated erase for Private deployment

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Before we progress the procurement checklist our InfoSec team needs a clear answer on a couple of operational items for the Private (VPC) deployment you propose:

1) Snapshots: if we instruct our infra team to take EBS/Snapshot-style backups of the model volumes, can those snapshots be restricted to a single AWS region and prevented from cross-region replication by Redwood? We need a guarantee that customer snapshots remain resident in the region we specify.

2) Customer-led erase: we want to own the process of permanently deleting tenant data (snapshots + attached volumes). What’s the exact sequence Redwood executes on a deletion request from our side? Will you accept a customer-signed wipe trigger, and can you provide a dated attestation after completion?

3) Evidence & SLA: we’ll need an attestation PDF and a timeline (RTO/RTA) for the erase operation. Our compliance team expects steps, logs, and the retention policy applied to snapshots to be documented.

Could you respond with the operational steps and point us to any templates for the attestation? I attached a short diagram of our planned snapshot cadence.

Thanks,
Diana Lee\Director, Cloud Architecture\MediCare Health

Hi Diana — thanks for laying this out. Looping in Marissa (Security & Compliance) and Evelyn (Private Deployments PM) to document the steps and confirm attestation mechanics. High-level answers below; Marissa will follow up with specifics and a draft attestation PDF you can use.

Summary (short):
- Snapshots: For Private deployments we do not initiate cross-region snapshot replication by default. Snapshots taken within the customer VPC/owner account remain in the AWS region where they were created unless your infra explicitly replicates them. For Redwood-managed storage options, we honor the "region lock" config at provisioning time; I'll have Evelyn add the config knobs to the runbook.
- Customer-led erase: We support a signed-trigger workflow: customer sends a signed erase request (DocuSign or our secure form), we perform a wipe sequence (delete snapshots, zero volumes, overwrite any cache copies, remove backups), capture deletion logs, and provide a timestamped attestation PDF.
- Evidence & SLA: We can commit to a documented timeline for the erase path for Private deployments in the US region: standard timeframe is 72 hours from acceptance of the signed trigger to final attestation. Extended SLAs available as part of Dedicated/Enterprise contracts.

Marissa / Evelyn — can you confirm the exact deletion steps we record, the log artifacts we provide, and attach a sample attestation? Diana, I'll also include a copy of the standard S3 snapshot policy template we hand to customers (editable).

Best,
Jonas Weber\Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference\jonas.weber@redwood.ai\Phone: +1 415 555 0123

Subject: Re: Questions on snapshots, regional retention, and customer-initiated erase for Private deployment

Hi Diana — thanks for the clear list. Adding the operational detail below (I tried to make this suitable for compliance review). If anything needs more detail, tell me which evidence items your auditors will want and we’ll include them in the attestation.

Operational model (Private/VPC):
- Storage ownership: For Private deployments we deploy with one of two storage models (customer-managed or Redwood-managed). For customer-managed mode: volumes and snapshots are created in the customer's AWS account (recommended). Redwood does not have control-plane level replication privileges in that account and cannot move snapshots between regions without explicit IAM action from the customer. For Redwood-managed mode we deploy storage in our account but honor an enforced region-lock configuration at provisioning time.

Snapshot residency guarantee:
- Customer-managed: residency is enforced by default because snapshots live in your AWS account and are subject to your region/replication policies.
- Redwood-managed: when you select a region-lock at provisioning, our orchestration disallows scheduled cross-region replication for those snapshot lifecycle policies. We document region-lock in the provisioning manifest and it is part of the deployment artifact.

Customer-initiated erase (recommended workflow):
1) Customer raises erase request via secure form or DocuSign with tenant identifier and scope (volumes, snapshots, audit logs).
2) Redwood validates request and acknowledges within 24 hours. Request ID issued.
3) Execution window scheduled (we aim for next maintenance window; if urgent we can escalate).
4) Delete steps executed:
   - Remove active mounts and detach volumes from hosts.
   - Delete snapshots (API delete-snapshot / S3 object delete for backups).
   - Overwrite (where supported) or re-provision volumes to ensure no residual plaintext (we document exact overwrite pattern used).
   - Purge any transient caches (KV caches, ephemeral nodes).
   - Remove metadata entries and wipe KV cache indices pointing to tenant objects.
5) For Redwood-managed backups we also remove any backup manifests and object indexes; for customer-managed we record the customer request ID and provide guidance for execution in your account if you prefer to run it yourselves.
6) Capture operational logs, audit events, and the deletion proof bundle (time-stamped logs + hash of deleted objects).
7) Issue attestation PDF signed by Redwood security lead with OSR (operation start) and OER (operation end) timestamps plus a checklist of actions taken.

Evidence we supply (standard bundle):
- Deletion request ID and DocuSign copy (if used).
- API call log excerpts (delete-snapshot, delete-object) with timestamps and ids.
- OS-level detach and wipe logs for affected hosts.
- Checksums/hashes for deleted snapshot manifests (where applicable).
- Attestation PDF (signed) that references the job run and includes the RTA.

RTO / timeline:
- Acknowledgement: within 24 hours of request.
- Target completion: default 72 hours from acknowledgement for US region Private deployments. Time may vary based on snapshot count and retained backup chains; we provide an ETA after validation.

Attestation template and policy artifacts attached: redwood_residency_attestation_v1.pdf and s3_snapshot_policy_template.txt. We can insert MediCare Health wording if you want company-specific language.

Notes about cross-region replication:
- If your environment has automated replication rules outside of Redwood control we cannot delete copies created by your replication engine; the attestation will note those objects and next steps on your side. If you want Redwood to fully manage replication and deletion we can include a replication-blocking IAM role as part of the onboarding.

If you’d like, we can run a dry-run using a test tenant and produce the attestation artifacts to demonstrate the workflow.

Regards,
Marissa Cole\Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference\marissa.cole@redwood.ai\Phone: +1 650 555 0182
